summary: Frontend-only verification of the new /dashboard design + mobile bottom navigation. Logged in as qa.coco.tester@example.com at 390x844 (mobile) and 1920x1080 (desktop). All 8 review items verified passing: login lands on /dashboard; on mobile top header is hidden and fixed bottom nav shows exactly [Dashboard, Live, Analyzer (raised center), Future, More] in order; on desktop 1920 bottom nav is hidden and top header is visible; bottom-nav Dashboard/Live/Future navigate to correct routes with active-item highlighting; Analyzer center button opens a sheet with OTC + Real Chart Analyzer links that navigate correctly; More sheet shows profile row, links (OTC, Real, News, Management, Landing page) + Log out button, and X close dismisses it; no horizontal overflow at 390 on /dashboard, /live-signals, /future-signals; new dark-purple dashboard renders profile card + Daily Limit + Trading tools without breakage at 390 and 1920.

detailed_checks.dashboard_bottom_padding_note: main has overflow-hidden and inner container uses pb-32 (128px), which is > bottom-nav height, so bottom nav does not cover content

critical_code_review_comments: CocoBottomNav is unconditionally rendered from TopNav. TopNav is imported on many app pages, so this is fine, but pages that do not include <TopNav /> would not get the bottom nav. Consider mounting CocoBottomNav in the app layout to guarantee it appears on every authenticated route.

main element in dashboard-content.tsx uses 'overflow-hidden' on a min-h-dvh container. This currently masks any horizontal overflow (scrollWidth == clientWidth) and can hide real overflow bugs during future edits — consider 'overflow-x-clip' only, or removing it, so overflow regressions surface in tests.
context_for_next_testing_agent: All 8 review items pass. Mobile bottom nav is delivered via <CocoBottomNav /> mounted at the end of TopNav (header itself is 'hidden md:block').
